ety.text: From Middle English durren, from Old English durran, from Proto-West Germanic *durʀan, from Proto-Germanic *durzaną (“to dare”), from Proto-Indo-European *dʰedʰórse (“to dare”), reduplicated stative of the root *dʰers- (“to be bold, to dare”), an *-s- extension of *dʰer- (“to hold, support”). senses.d: To have enough courage (to do something).

senses.d: To defy or challenge (someone to do something).

senses.d: To have enough courage to meet or do something, go somewhere, etc.; to face up to.
ex: Will you dare death to reach your goal?
